extra.message: parseFile() builds a shell command by string-concatenating phpPath, realFileName, arg1 and arg2, then passes it to child_process.exec(). arg1/arg2 (and fileName, via realFileName) originate from routes/php.js as raw, un-sanitized substrings pulled directly out of request.originalUrl. An attacker can embed shell metacharacters (e.g. `;`, `|`, backticks, `$()`) in the 'item' or 'price' query values (or in the .php path itself) to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server.

The wildcard route '*.php' extracts the path and 'item'/'price' values directly from request.originalUrl via raw substr() slicing (no decodeURIComponent, no whitelist/sanitization) and forwards them unmodified into execPHP.parseFile(), which shells out via child_process.exec (see execphp.js:22-23). This is the attacker-controlled entry point for the command injection sink.

realFileName is built by concatenating the fixed phpFolder ('./phpFiles/') with the attacker-controlled fileName (derived from the request path in routes/php.js, matched by the '*.php' wildcard route) with no normalization or traversal check. A URL like '/../../etc/somefile.php' lets an attacker point the exec()'d command at arbitrary files outside phpFiles/.

collection.findOne({ username: req.body.username, password: req.body.password }) passes request-body values directly as MongoDB query operands. Because express.json() is enabled (app.js:36), an attacker can send a JSON body such as {"username":{"$ne":null},"password":{"$ne":null}} (or $gt/$regex operators) instead of strings, causing the query to match any document and bypass authentication without knowing valid credentials.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: GET /users/userlist returns every field of every user document (collection.find({},{})) with no authentication or authorization check and no field projection. Any unauthenticated caller can dump the full user list, including password and credit-card fields, since this router is mounted at '/users' in app.js with no auth middleware in front of it.

DELETE /users/deleteuser/:id removes the user document matching the supplied :id with no authentication and no check that the caller owns that account. Any unauthenticated client can delete an arbitrary user by ID (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: POST /users/adduser creates a new account from the raw request body with no authentication check, allowing anyone to register accounts (used later as an unauthenticated injection point into the admin user list rendered by public/javascripts/global.js).

populateTable() concatenates this.username, this.email and this._id (returned verbatim from the unauthenticated /users/userlist endpoint, itself populated from the unauthenticated /users/adduser endpoint) directly into an HTML string, which is then injected via $('.userList table tbody').html(tableContent). Since usernames/emails are attacker-controlled and never HTML-escaped, an attacker can register a user whose username contains a script/img-onerror payload to achieve stored XSS against the admin viewing '/admin'.

The express-session secret used to sign session-ID cookies is a hardcoded string literal ('Shh, its a secret!') committed to source control. Anyone with access to the repo can forge valid session cookies.

GET /users returns the entire req.session.user object, which was populated straight from the MongoDB user document (routes/users.js:65) and therefore includes the plaintext password and credit-card fields. This information is sent to the client on every session check.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The express-session configuration sets no 'cookie' options (secure, sameSite), so the session cookie is transmitted over plain HTTP and lacks SameSite protection; combined with resave/saveUninitialized both true, this increases exposure to session hijacking and unnecessary session-store writes.
